::: notes
"Tip the sets into the bin and you lose nothing you can hold. Every brick is still there. What's gone is everything about them."

1:40.

Open on the title: "Every brick fits. Build the castle any time." That's CDISC's win, said generously.

Click: the title turns to "Good luck finding the castle later." as the camera zooms into the bin. A half-built castle, a half-built ship with something stuck on it, a crumpled booklet. "This is how my kids leave their Lego." Then the questions nobody can answer:

- Which pieces made the castle, and which edition of the instructions.
- Whether anyone changed the ship after it was built.
- How to rebuild the 2019 castle exactly, today.
- Which parts of a new build came from which set.

"That's snapshot identity, versions and lineage."

The turn: "Sort the bin by colour and it's perfectly tidy. The sets are still gone." This is not a tidying problem, so no amount of sorting fixes it.

Click: "CDISC made every brick fit. Nothing keeps the sets."

Say "snapshot identity"; CDISC already gives semantic traceability. No jokes about SAS or SCEs here.
:::
